title: Horse Rug for Bedroom: Sizes, Placement and Prices (50)
meta_description: Pick a horse rug for your bedroom by bed width and floor space. Compare sizes from $21.90 to $134.90, every design with a non-slip backing. (141)
body_html:
The right horse rug for a bedroom depends on two things: how wide your bed is and where you want something soft underfoot. Chillgen's horse area rugs come in sizes from 24"x36" to 60"x96", starting at $29.90 for the smallest and $134.90 for the largest. Smaller mats start at $21.90.

A quick note on the term: riders also say "horse rug" for horse covers, the blankets a horse wears in the field. This page is about the other kind, floor rugs with horse designs on them.

On this page

  1. What size horse rug fits a bedroom?
  2. Where should a horse rug go in a bedroom?
  3. Worked example: one bed, three ways to cover the floor
  4. Will a horse area rug slip or feel thin underfoot?
  5. Which horse rugs suit your bedroom's colors?
  6. Can a bedroom horse rug work in the living room too?

What size horse rug fits a bedroom?

The Horse Rugs collection has 28 products and two size menus. The area-rug designs come in 24"x36", 36"x60", 48"x72" and 60"x96". The smaller mat designs come in 16x16, 16x24, 20x32 and 24x36 inches. The prices below are the lowest starting price for each size across the whole collection, so a particular design may cost more.

Both menus include a 24 x 36 size, with different starting prices. The listing details we have don't say what else separates the two, so check the product page of the design you like before you compare them.

How to apply it: measure your bed's width and the floor on each side of it, out to the nearest wall or piece of furniture. Then find the smallest row in the table that covers the spot you actually step on. You can compare designs at each size in the Horse Rugs collection.

What to check

  • Your bed frame's width, not just the mattress width
  • Clear floor between the bed and the nearest wall or dresser
  • Which size menu the design you like uses
  • The price for your size on that product page, not just the "from" price

Where should a horse rug go in a bedroom?

A bedroom rug usually goes in one of three places, and each one needs a different size.

Under the lower part of the bed, crosswise. The rug runs side to side under the bottom of the bed, with an equal strip showing on each side. It's the only one of the three placements where a single rug sits under both sleepers' feet. Of the sizes here, 60"x96" is the one with enough length to do it.

Beside the bed. A 36"x60" runner, or a small mat from 16x24 to 24x36 inches, sits where your feet land. Two sleepers need two of them.

At the foot of the bed. A 48"x72" rug sits across the foot of the bed. It suits a bed with a bench or storage chest there, and it's the spot you see first from the door.

How to apply it: before you order, mark the rug's outline on the floor at full size with painter's tape. Walk your usual path into bed, then open the door and any drawers that face the bed. A taped outline shows things the product photos can't, like a door that catches the rug's edge.

What to check

  • Whether the door swings clear of the taped outline
  • Whether wardrobe or dresser drawers open over it
  • How far the rug reaches past the bed on each side
  • Whether you need one rug or a matching pair

Worked example: one bed, three ways to cover the floor

This is a made-up bedroom used to show the method. It isn't a customer's room. Say the mattress is 60 inches wide and there's floor space on both sides of the bed. Two people sleep in it, and both want something soft when they get up.

Option A: one 60"x96" rug, crosswise. The 96-inch side runs across the bed. That makes the rug 36 inches wider than the mattress (96 minus 60), and the extra width is split between the two sides. Cost: from $134.90.

Option B: two 36"x60" runners, one per side. Each runner runs 60 inches along the side of the bed. Cost: two runners at the $64.90 starting price, which comes to slightly less than Option A.

Option C: one 48"x72" rug at the foot. Its 72-inch side is only a little wider than the mattress, so it barely reaches past either side. Neither person's bedside is covered. Cost: from $99.90.

The decision. Option C is out, because it doesn't put rug where either person gets out of bed. A and B are close on price, so the room decides. This couple picks A because it's one rug covering both sides, and that's one thing to clean instead of two. A couple whose nightstands sit tight against the bed might pick B, because a runner doesn't have to fit under the nightstand legs.

What to check for your own room

  • Your actual mattress and frame width in place of 60 inches
  • That half of the extra width is enough to step onto on each side
  • Current prices for your chosen design at both sizes
  • Where the nightstands sit relative to the rug's edge

Will a horse area rug slip or feel thin underfoot?

Here's what the product pages say, and how many of the 28 say it:

  • Non-slip backing: "Non-slip underside backing for enhanced floor grip," on all 28 product pages.
  • Cushioning: "Soft memory foam cushion helps relieve foot pressure," on 24 of 28 pages.
  • Low pile: "Easy-care, stain-resistant low pile material," on 14 of 28 pages.

So every horse rug in the collection lists a non-slip backing. Cushioning isn't universal, because not every product page mentions memory foam. If a soft first step out of bed is why you're buying, look for that line on the product page before you order.

Low pile helps in a bedroom for a practical reason. A flatter surface is easier for a door, a rolling laundry basket or a nightstand leg to pass over. The product pages call the pile low but don't give a height, so check the gap under your bedroom door if the rug will sit near it.

How to apply it: note what floor the rug will sit on. The backing is described as gripping "the floor," and the product pages don't say how it behaves over carpet. If you plan to lay the rug on carpet, ask the shop before ordering.

What to check

  • The memory foam line on the product page of your chosen design
  • Your floor type: wood, tile, vinyl or carpet
  • Clearance under the bedroom door, if the rug sits near it
  • Whether your nightstand or bed legs will rest on the rug's edge

Which horse rugs suit your bedroom's colors?

Fourteen product pages describe the print as "printed with premium heat dye sublimation." The designs below are a starting point, grouped by the kind of room each is likely to suit.

  • A black and white bedroom, or one with a lot of grey: the black and white horse rug, from $64.90
  • A softer room with patterned bedding: the floral horse herd rug, from $64.90
  • A room that already has purple in the bedding or on the walls: the purple horse area rug, from $64.90
  • A room that needs one bold close-up as its focal point: the horse eye area rug, from $64.90
  • A western room on a smaller budget: the chestnut running horse rug, from $29.90
  • A room with patterned textiles or geometric prints: the tribal horse area rug, from $64.90

Twenty-one product pages list "Customizable sizes to fit various living spaces." The size menus in the table are the options shown on the product pages. If you need something outside them, ask the shop before ordering.

How to apply it: hold the product photo next to your bedding and pick one color they share. A rug usually sits better in a room when it repeats a color that's already there.

What to check

  • One color the rug shares with your bedding or curtains
  • How much of the design the bed will hide (Option A above)
  • Whether the design reads the right way up from the door
  • Which size menu that design offers

Can a bedroom horse rug work in the living room too?

Yes, as far as size goes. The largest option, 60"x96", is big enough to sit in front of a sofa or under a coffee table. For horse rugs in a living room, the claim to check is how the rug handles traffic. Six of the 28 product pages say the rug is "Easy to clean and maintain for high-traffic areas," and 14 describe the low pile as stain-resistant.

A living room gets shoes, spills and more feet than a bedroom does. Before you move a bedroom horse area rug into a busier room, read the cleaning line on that rug's product page. If the page doesn't give care instructions, ask the shop how to clean it before the first spill, not after.

How to apply it: in a living room, measure the seating area instead of a bed. Measure the sofa's width, then the distance from the sofa to the coffee table. Whether a 60"x96" rug laid lengthwise in front of the sofa reaches under the coffee table depends on how far apart the two sit.

What to check

  • The "high-traffic" cleaning line on that product's page
  • The sofa's width against the rug's 96-inch side
  • Whether the sofa's front legs will sit on the rug or off it
  • How to clean the rug, confirmed before you need to

Once you have your measurements and a placement, you can compare all 28 horse rug designs in your size.
